faqs.q: Do you need a permit for a commercial roof replacement in Bloomfield, NJ?

runs.v: Yes. The 25% rule in N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 sets the line: a commercial, multi-family, or attached building needs a construction permit once roof work exceeds 25% of the total roof area in a 12-month period, so a full commercial replacement always needs one, while Bloomfield homeowners with a detached one- or two-family house can reroof, even with a full tear-off, as ordinary maintenance with no permit. Confirm filing details with the Bloomfield construction office before work begins.

faqs.q: When should a Bloomfield commercial roof be replaced rather than repaired?

runs.v: Replace it when membrane damage exceeds 25 to 30% of the roof area, when leaks recur at the same location, or when core samples show saturated insulation across most of the roof; the 25 to 30% threshold comes from Modernize and HomeGuide flat-roof guidance, and a recurring same-spot leak signals systemic failure, per HomeAdvisor. Localized damage on a dry roof favors repair services, confirmed by an ASTM C1153 infrared moisture survey.

faqs.q: Does a Bloomfield historic-district building need extra approval for a roof replacement?

runs.v: It can. A building inside a historic district can need extra review for exterior roofing work, separate from the construction permit, so confirm current requirements with the Bloomfield construction office before work begins. Per the National Park Service, National Register listing alone places no federal restriction on a private property owner.

faqs.q: What new roof system fits a Bloomfield commercial or garden-apartment flat roof?

runs.v: It depends on the building, the drainage, and the rooftop exposure. TPO and EPDM are the most common choices for commercial buildings, PVC resists rooftop grease and chemical exposure, modified bitumen handles foot traffic, built-up roofing suits heavy industrial decks, and white PVC and TPO carry high solar reflectance for a Broad Street or Bloomfield Avenue building.

faqs.q: How does a commercial roof replacement handle drainage on a flat Bloomfield roof?

runs.v: A replacement builds tapered insulation to at least ¼ inch per foot of slope so the flat roof sheds water rather than ponding, per the NRCA and ARMA. The tear-off exposes the deck once, the point at which the drainage correction goes in at the lowest added labor on Watsessing's low-lying blocks and the Broad Street and Garden State Parkway corridors.
